metadata.title: What Can We Learn Privately?
metadata.authors: Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan, Homin K. Lee, Kobbi Nissim, Sofya Raskhodnikova, Adam Smith
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-Differential Privacy
nodes.statement: A randomized algorithm $A$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private if for all neighboring databases $z, z'$ and all sets $S$ of outputs, $\Pr[A(z) \in S] \leq \exp(\epsilon) \cdot \Pr[A(z') \in S]$.
nodes.statement_clean: An algorithm is differentially private if its output distribution changes by at most a multiplicative $e^{\epsilon}$ factor when one database entry is changed.

nodes.name: Composition and Post-processing
nodes.statement: If $A$ runs $k$ algorithms $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ where each $A_i$ is $\epsilon_i$-differentially private and outputs a function of the results, then $A$ is $(\sum_{i=1}^{k} \epsilon_i)$-differentially private.
conclusions: $A$ is $(\sum_{i=1}^{k} \epsilon_i)$-differentially private

nodes.name: Laplace Mechanism (Global Sensitivity)
nodes.statement: For $f : D^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with global sensitivity $GS_f = \max_{z,z'} |f(z)-f(z')|$ over neighbors, the algorithm that returns $f(z) + \eta$ with $\eta \sim \mathrm{Lap}(GS_f/\epsilon)$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private.
conclusions: Outputting $f(z) + \eta$ with $\eta \sim \mathrm{Lap}(GS_f/\epsilon)$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private

nodes.name: PAC Learning
nodes.statement: Class $C$ is PAC learnable using $H$ if there is an algorithm $A$ and polynomial $\mathrm{poly}(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)$ such that for all $d$, $c \in C_d$, distributions $X$ on $X_d$, and $\alpha,\beta \in (0,1/2)$, given $n = \mathrm{poly}(d, 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta))$ examples, $A$ outputs $h \in H$ with $\Pr[\mathrm{err}(h) \leq \alpha] \geq 1 - \beta$.

nodes.name: Agnostic Learning
nodes.statement: Defined like PAC learning except (i) data drawn from an arbitrary distribution $D$ on $X_d \times Y_d$, and (ii) the output satisfies $\Pr[\mathrm{err}(h) \leq OPT + \alpha] \geq 1-\beta$ where $OPT = \min_{f \in C_d}\{\mathrm{err}(f)\}$.

nodes.name: Private PAC Learning
nodes.statement: Concept class $C$ is privately PAC learnable using $H$ if there exists $A$ taking $\epsilon, \alpha, \beta, z$ with $n$ polynomial in $1/\epsilon, d, 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta)$ such that (a) $A(\epsilon,\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private and (b) $A$ PAC learns $C$ using $H$.

nodes.name: Private Agnostic Learning
nodes.statement: Defined analogously to private PAC learning, with the agnostic learning utility condition replacing the PAC utility condition.

nodes.name: Generic Private Agnostic Learner $A_q$ (Exponential Mechanism)
nodes.statement: Output hypothesis $h \in H_d$ with probability proportional to $\exp\!\left(\epsilon\, q(z,h)/2\right)$, where $q(z,h) = -|\{i : y_i \neq h(x_i)\}|$ is minus the empirical misclassification count.
output: A hypothesis $h \in H_d$ sampled with probability $\propto \exp(\epsilon\, q(z,h)/2)$

nodes.name: Privacy of $A_q$
nodes.statement: The algorithm $A_q$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private.
conclusions: $A_q$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private

nodes.name: Generic Private Learner
nodes.statement: For all $d$, any concept class $C_d$ with $|C_d| \leq \exp(\mathrm{poly}(d))$ is privately agnostically learnable using $H_d = C_d$ with $n = O\!\left((\ln |H_d| + \ln \tfrac{1}{\beta}) \cdot \max\{\tfrac{1}{\epsilon\alpha}, \tfrac{1}{\alpha^2}\}\right)$ labeled examples.
conclusions: Class $C_d$ is privately agnostically learnable using $H_d = C_d$
Sample complexity $n = O\!\left((\ln |H_d| + \ln(1/\beta)) \cdot \max\{1/(\epsilon\alpha), 1/\alpha^2\}\right)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4 (Generic Private Learner)
nodes.statement: Privacy is by Lemma 3.3. For utility, apply Chernoff-Hoeffding to bound deviation between true and training error uniformly over $H_d$, then bound the probability that $A_q$ outputs a high-error hypothesis using the exponential mechanism's selection probabilities.

nodes.name: Privacy from Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: Lemma 3.3 directly gives $\epsilon$-differential privacy of $A_q$.

nodes.name: Uniform deviation bound on training error
nodes.statement: By Chernoff-Hoeffding (Theorem A.2), $\Pr[|\mathrm{err}(h) - \mathrm{err}_T(h)| \geq \rho] \leq 2\exp(-2n\rho^2)$, and a union bound over $h \in H_d$ gives $2|H_d|\exp(-2n\rho^2)$.

nodes.name: Bound on output probability via exponential mechanism
nodes.statement: Conditioned on uniform $\rho$-closeness, the probability that $A_q(z)$ outputs $h$ with $\mathrm{err}_T(h) \geq OPT + 2\rho$ is at most $|H_d|\exp(-\epsilon n \rho /2)$.

nodes.name: Choose $\rho = \alpha/3$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $\rho = \alpha/3$ and $n \geq \tfrac{6}{\epsilon}(\ln |H_d| + \ln \tfrac{1}{\beta}) \cdot \max\{\tfrac{1}{\alpha}, \tfrac{1}{\alpha^2}\}$ gives $\Pr[E] \leq \beta$.

nodes.name: VC dimension
nodes.statement: A set $S \subseteq X_d$ is shattered by $C_d$ if $C_d$ restricted to $S$ contains all $2^{|S|}$ functions $S \to \{0,1\}$. $VCDIM(C_d)$ is the cardinality of the largest such $S$.

nodes.name: Private Agnostic Learner with VC Sample Bound
nodes.statement: Every concept class $C_d$ is privately agnostically learnable using $H_d = C_d$ with $n = O\!\left((VCDIM(C_d) \cdot \ln |X_d| + \ln \tfrac{1}{\beta}) \cdot \max\{\tfrac{1}{\epsilon\alpha}, \tfrac{1}{\alpha^2}\}\right)$ labeled examples.
conclusions: Sample complexity $n = O\!\left((VCDIM(C_d)\ln|X_d| + \ln(1/\beta)) \cdot \max\{1/(\epsilon\alpha), 1/\alpha^2\}\right)$

nodes.name: PARITY
nodes.statement: PARITY is the class of parity functions $c_r : \{0,1\}^d \to \{0,1\}$ indexed by $r \in \{0,1\}^d$, where $c_r(x) = r \odot x$ denotes inner product modulo $2$.

nodes.name: Private Learner for PARITY, $A(z, \epsilon)$
nodes.statement: Constant-success-probability private PAC learner for PARITY: with probability $1/2$ output $\bot$; otherwise sample $S$ by including each index with probability $p = \epsilon/4$, solve the linear system on $S$ via Gaussian elimination, and output a uniformly random consistent parity (or $\bot$ if infeasible).

nodes.name: Output $\bot$ with probability $1/2$
nodes.statement: With probability $1/2$, output $\bot$ and terminate.

nodes.name: Subsample indices
nodes.statement: Construct $S$ by picking each $i \in [n]$ independently with probability $p = \epsilon/4$.

nodes.name: Solve linear system on $S$
nodes.statement: Use Gaussian elimination to solve $\{x_i \odot r = c_r(x_i) : i \in S\}$; let $V_S$ be the resulting affine subspace.

nodes.name: Sample uniform $r^* \in V_S$
nodes.statement: Pick $r^* \in V_S$ uniformly at random and output $c_{r^*}$; if $V_S = \emptyset$, output $\bot$.

nodes.name: Utility of $A$ (PARITY learner)
nodes.statement: If $z = (z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ with $z_i = (x_i, c(x_i))$, $x_i$ i.i.d. from $X$ on $\{0,1\}^d$, $c \in \mathrm{PARITY}$, and $n \geq \tfrac{8}{\alpha\epsilon}(d\ln 2 + \ln 4)$, then $\Pr[A(z,\epsilon) = h \text{ with err}(h) \leq \alpha] \geq 1/4$.
conclusions: $\Pr[A(z,\epsilon)=h \text{ with err}(h) \leq \alpha] \geq 1/4$

nodes.name: Privacy of $A$ (PARITY learner)
nodes.statement: Algorithm $A$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private.
assumptions: $A$ as defined above with sampling probability $p = \epsilon/4$ and $\epsilon \leq 1/2$
conclusions: $A$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private

nodes.name: Conditional ratio bound
nodes.statement: For all $z \in D^n$ and all $h \in \mathrm{PARITY}$: $\dfrac{\Pr[A(z) = h \mid i \in S]}{\Pr[A(z) = h \mid i \notin S]} \leq 2$.

nodes.name: Amplified Private PAC Learner for PARITY, $A^*(z,\epsilon,\alpha,\beta)$
nodes.statement: Repeat the base learner $A$ on $k$ disjoint subsamples, then select the candidate with smallest perturbed training error (Laplace noise added) on a held-out test set.

nodes.name: Set parameters
nodes.statement: Set $\beta' \leftarrow \beta/2$, $\alpha' \leftarrow \alpha/5$, $k \leftarrow \lceil \log_{4/3}(1/\beta') \rceil$, $n_0 \leftarrow cd/(\alpha'\epsilon)$, $s \leftarrow (c'k/(\alpha'\epsilon))\log(k/\beta')$.

nodes.name: Check sample size
nodes.statement: If $n \leq k n_0 + s$, stop and return ``insufficient samples''.

nodes.name: Split into training and test sets
nodes.statement: Divide $z$ into $\bar z = (z_1,\ldots,z_{kn_0})$ and $\hat z = (z_{kn_0+1},\ldots,z_{kn_0+s})$, then partition $\bar z$ into $k$ blocks of size $n_0$.

nodes.name: Run base learner on each block, perturb errors
nodes.statement: For $j = 1,\ldots,k$, set $h_j \leftarrow A(\bar z_j, \epsilon)$ and compute perturbed test error $\widehat{\mathrm{err}}_T(h_j) = \tfrac{|\{z_i \in \hat z : h_j(x_i) \neq c(x_i)\}|}{s} + \mathrm{Lap}(k/(\epsilon s))$.

nodes.name: Output minimum-error candidate
nodes.statement: Output $h^* = h_{j^*}$ where $j^* = \arg\min_{j\in[k]} \widehat{\mathrm{err}}_T(h_j)$.

nodes.name: Efficient Private PAC Learning of PARITY
nodes.statement: Algorithm $A^*$ efficiently and privately PAC learns $\mathrm{PARITY}$ (Definition 3.1) with $O\!\left(\dfrac{d\log(1/\beta)}{\epsilon\alpha}\right)$ samples.
conclusions: $A^*$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private and PAC learns $\mathrm{PARITY}$ with sample complexity $O(d\log(1/\beta)/(\epsilon\alpha))$

nodes.name: Privacy of $A^*$
nodes.statement: Algorithm $A^*$ is $\epsilon$-differentially private.

nodes.name: Utility of $A^*$
nodes.statement: $A^*(\cdot,\epsilon,\cdot,\cdot)$ PAC learns $\mathrm{PARITY}$ with sample complexity $n = O\!\left(\dfrac{d\log(1/\beta)}{\epsilon\alpha}\right)$.

nodes.name: Local Randomizer
nodes.statement: An $\epsilon$-local randomizer $R : D \to W$ is an $\epsilon$-differentially private algorithm taking a database of size $n=1$: $\Pr[R(u)=w] \leq e^{\epsilon}\Pr[R(u')=w]$ for all $u,u' \in D$ and $w \in W$.

nodes.name: LR Oracle
nodes.statement: For database $z = (z_1,\ldots,z_n)$, the oracle $LR_z(\cdot,\cdot)$ takes $i \in [n]$ and an $\epsilon$-local randomizer $R$ and returns a sample from $R(z_i)$.

nodes.name: Local Algorithm
nodes.statement: An algorithm is $\epsilon$-local if it accesses $z$ only via $LR_z$, with the restriction that for each $i$, the sum of privacy parameters of all randomizers applied to $z_i$ is at most $\epsilon$. Local algorithms preparing all queries in advance are noninteractive; otherwise interactive.

nodes.name: SQ Oracle
nodes.statement: For a distribution $D$ over $\mathbf{D}$, the SQ oracle $SQ_D$ takes $g : \mathbf{D} \to \{+1,-1\}$ and tolerance $\tau \in (0,1)$ and outputs $v$ with $|v - \mathbb{E}_{u \sim D}[g(u)]| \leq \tau$.

nodes.name: SQ Algorithm
nodes.statement: An SQ algorithm accesses the distribution $D$ via $SQ_D$. SQ algorithms preparing all queries in advance are nonadaptive; otherwise adaptive.

nodes.name: Local Algorithm $A_g$ Simulating an SQ Query
nodes.statement: For an SQ query $g : D \to [-b,b]$, output $\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n LR_z(i, R_g)$ where $R_g(u) = g(u) + \eta$, $\eta \sim \mathrm{Lap}(2b/\epsilon)$.

nodes.name: Accuracy of Local SQ Simulation
nodes.statement: If $z$ has $n \geq c \cdot \dfrac{\log(1/\beta) b^2}{\epsilon^2 \tau^2}$ entries i.i.d.\ from $D$, then $A_g$ approximates $\mathbb{E}_{u \sim D}[g(u)]$ within $\pm \tau$ with probability at least $1-\beta$.
assumptions: $n \geq c \log(1/\beta) b^2/(\epsilon^2 \tau^2)$ for sufficiently large constant $c$
conclusions: $A_g$ outputs an estimate within $\pm \tau$ of $\mathbb{E}_{u \sim D}[g(u)]$ with probability $\geq 1-\beta$

nodes.name: Local Simulation of SQ
nodes.statement: Any SQ algorithm $A_{SQ}$ making $\leq t$ queries with tolerance $\geq \tau$ can be simulated by an $\epsilon$-differentially private local algorithm using $n \geq c \cdot \dfrac{t \log(t/\beta) b^2}{\epsilon^2 \tau^2}$ i.i.d.\ samples; the simulation is noninteractive iff $A_{SQ}$ is nonadaptive, and efficient iff $A_{SQ}$ is efficient.
assumptions: SQ algorithm $A_{SQ}$ makes $\leq t$ queries with tolerance $\geq \tau$
conclusions: The local simulation gives the same output as $A_{SQ}$ with probability $\geq 1-\beta$
It is $\epsilon$-differentially private
Noninteractive iff $A_{SQ}$ nonadaptive; efficient iff $A_{SQ}$ efficient

nodes.name: SQ Simulation of Local Algorithms
nodes.statement: For every noninteractive (resp.\ interactive) $\epsilon$-local algorithm $A$ making $t$ queries to $LR_z$, there is a nonadaptive (resp.\ adaptive) SQ algorithm $B$ making $O(t \cdot e^{\epsilon})$ expected queries to $SQ_D$ with accuracy $\tau = \Theta(\beta/(e^{2\epsilon} t))$ such that the statistical difference between $B$'s and $A$'s output distributions is at most $\beta$.
conclusions: $B$ makes $O(t e^{\epsilon})$ expected SQ queries with $\tau = \Theta(\beta/(e^{2\epsilon}t))$
Statistical difference between outputs of $B$ and $A$ is $\leq \beta$

nodes.name: Noninteractive-to-Nonadaptive SQ Simulation
nodes.statement: For every noninteractive local $A$ making $t$ queries to $LR_z$, there is a nonadaptive SQ $B$ making $t e^{\epsilon}$ expected queries with accuracy $\tau = \Theta(\beta/(e^{2\epsilon} t))$ and output statistical distance $\leq \beta$ from $A$.

nodes.name: Interactive-to-Adaptive SQ Simulation
nodes.statement: For every interactive local $A$ making $t$ queries to $LR_z$, there is an adaptive SQ $B$ making $O(t e^{\epsilon})$ expected queries with accuracy $\tau = \Theta(\beta/(e^{2\epsilon} t))$ and output statistical distance $\leq \beta$ from $A$.

nodes.name: $B_{R,\epsilon}$: SQ Simulation of an $\epsilon$-Local Randomizer
nodes.statement: Rejection-sampling simulation of $R$: sample $w \sim R(0)$, estimate $p(w)$ via an SQ query $g(z_i) = (\Pr[R(z_i)=w] - q(w))/(q(w)(e^{\epsilon}-e^{-\epsilon}))$, accept $w$ with probability $\tilde p(w)/(q(w)(1+\beta/(3t))e^{\epsilon})$, else repeat.

nodes.name: Local Learning
nodes.statement: Locally learnable is defined like privately PAC learnable, with the additional requirement that for all $\epsilon > 0$, $A(\epsilon,\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)$ is $\epsilon$-local and invokes $LR_z$ at most $\mathrm{poly}(d, \mathrm{size}(c), 1/\epsilon, 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta))$ times.

nodes.name: SQ Learning
nodes.statement: SQ learnable is defined like PAC learnable except that, instead of accessing examples directly, an SQ learner $A$ makes $\mathrm{poly}(d, \mathrm{size}(c), 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta))$ queries to $SQ_{c,X}$ with tolerance $\tau \geq 1/\mathrm{poly}(d,\mathrm{size}(c), 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta))$.

nodes.name: Transparent Local Randomizer
nodes.statement: An $\epsilon$-local randomizer $R : D \to W$ is transparent if (i) the time to evaluate $R$ on any $u \in D$ and (ii) the time to compute $\Pr[R(u) = w]$ for any $u \in D, w \in W$ are polynomial in the input size and $1/\epsilon$.

nodes.name: Equivalence of Local and SQ Learning
nodes.statement: Concept class $C$ is locally learnable using $H$ by an interactive local learner with access to $LR_z$ iff $C$ is SQ learnable using $H$ by an adaptive SQ learner with access to $SQ_{c,X}$. The simulations preserve efficiency (modulo transparency) and adaptivity/interactivity.
conclusions: Interactive local learnability of $C$ $\iff$ adaptive SQ learnability of $C$
Efficient SQ $\Leftrightarrow$ efficient local with transparent randomizers
Nonadaptive SQ $\Leftrightarrow$ noninteractive local

nodes.name: Local Learning $\subsetneq$ Private PAC Learning
nodes.statement: Concept classes learnable by local learners are a strict subset of concept classes PAC learnable privately, both with and without computational restrictions.

nodes.name: MASKED-PARITY
nodes.statement: MASKED-PARITY is the class of $c_{r,a} : \{0,1\}^d \times \{0,1\}^{\log d} \times \{0,1\} \to \{+1,-1\}$ with $c_{r,a}(x,i,b) = (-1)^{r \odot x + a}$ if $b=0$ and $(-1)^{r_i}$ if $b=1$, indexed by $r \in \{0,1\}^d$ and $a \in \{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Adaptive SQ Learner $A_{MP}$ for MASKED-PARITY
nodes.statement: Two-round adaptive SQ learner: round 1 issues $d$ queries $g_j$ extracting bits $\hat r_j$ from the $b=1$ half, then round 2 issues a query $g_{d+1}$ to recover $\hat a$ from the $b=0$ half using $\hat r$.
input: SQ oracle $SQ_D$ over uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^{d+\log d + 1}$

nodes.name: Round 1: extract bits of $r$
nodes.statement: For $j = 1,\ldots,d$ in parallel, define $g_j(x,i,b,y) = (i=j) \wedge (b=1) \wedge (y=-1)$, query $\mathrm{answer}_j \leftarrow SQ_D(g_j, \tau)$ with $\tau = 1/(4d+1)$, and set $\hat r_j = 1$ if $\mathrm{answer}_j > 1/(4d)$ else $0$.

nodes.name: Round 2: recover $a$ and output
nodes.statement: Set $\hat r = \hat r_1 \ldots \hat r_d$, define $g_{d+1}(x,i,b,y) = (b=0) \wedge (y \neq (-1)^{\hat r \odot x})$, query $\mathrm{answer}_{d+1} \leftarrow SQ_D(g_{d+1}, 1/5)$, set $\hat a = 1$ if $\mathrm{answer}_{d+1} > 1/4$ else $0$, and output $c_{\hat r, \hat a}$.

nodes.name: Adaptive SQ Learner Correctness for MASKED-PARITY
nodes.statement: Algorithm $A_{MP}$ efficiently learns MASKED-PARITY with probability $1$ in $2$ rounds using $d+1$ SQ queries over the uniform distribution with minimum tolerance $1/(4d+1)$.
assumptions: Examples drawn from the uniform distribution on $\{0,1\}^{d+\log d+1}$
conclusions: $A_{MP}$ outputs the target $c_{r,a}$ with probability $1$ using $d+1$ adaptive SQ queries with tolerance $\geq 1/(4d+1)$

nodes.name: Adaptive vs.\ Nonadaptive SQ Separation via MASKED-PARITY
nodes.statement: (1) There is an efficient adaptive SQ learner for MASKED-PARITY over the uniform distribution. (2) No nonadaptive SQ learner with $t$ queries of tolerance $\geq 2^{-d/3}$ over the uniform distribution outputs $h$ with $\mathrm{err}(c_{\bar r, \bar a}, h) < 1/4$ better than with probability $1 - \tfrac{1}{2}(1 - t/2^{d/3+2})$ over uniform $(\bar r, \bar a)$.
assumptions: Examples drawn from the uniform distribution
conclusions: MASKED-PARITY is efficiently learnable by adaptive SQ
No nonadaptive SQ learner with $t$ queries and tolerance $\geq 2^{-d/3}$ achieves error $<1/4$ except with probability $\leq \tfrac{1}{2}(1 - t/2^{d/3+2})$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.16, part (2) (Nonadaptive lower bound)
nodes.statement: Decompose any SQ query into label-independent and label-dependent parts using Fourier analysis; show that for typical $(\bar r, \bar a)$ the $b=0$ inner product $|\langle f_g^0, c_{\bar r,\bar a}^0 \rangle|$ is $\leq 2^{-d/3}$, so an SQ oracle can answer all queries independently of $\bar a$, forcing the learner to err on at least $1/4$ of the domain.

nodes.name: Decompose SQ query via $f_g$ and $C_g$
nodes.statement: Write $f_g(x,i,b) = (g(x,i,b,1) - g(x,i,b,-1))/2$ and $C_g = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}[g(x,i,b,1) + g(x,i,b,-1)]$, so $\mathbb{E}[g(x,i,b,c_{\bar r,\bar a})] = C_g + \langle f_g, c_{\bar r,\bar a} \rangle$.

nodes.name: Split inner product by $b \in \{0,1\}$
nodes.statement: Define $f_g^s, c_{\bar r,\bar a}^s$ restricting to $b=s$, giving $\langle f_g, c_{\bar r,\bar a}\rangle = \langle f_g^0, c_{\bar r,\bar a}^0\rangle + \langle f_g^1, c_{\bar r,\bar a}^1\rangle$, with only the $b=0$ term depending on $\bar a$.

nodes.name: Orthogonality and Bessel-type bound
nodes.statement: Show $\{c_{r,0}^0\}_r$ and $\{c_{r,1}^0\}_r$ are orthogonal sets with $\|c_{r,a}^0\| = 1/\sqrt 2$, so $\sum_{(r,a)} 2 \langle f_g^0, c_{r,a}^0\rangle^2 \leq 1$ and at most $2^{2d/3-1}$ functions $c_{r,a}$ have $|\langle f_g^0, c_{r,a}^0\rangle| \geq 2^{-d/3}$.

nodes.name: Union bound over $t$ queries
nodes.statement: For uniform $(\bar r, \bar a)$ and $t$ queries, $\Pr[\mathrm{Good}] \geq 1 - t/2^{d/3+2}$, where Good means all queries can be answered without dependence on $\bar a$.

nodes.name: Force $\geq 1/4$ error via $a$ flip
nodes.statement: Since $c_{\bar r,0}(x,i,0) = -c_{\bar r,1}(x,i,0)$, for any output $h$ at least one $\bar a$ gives error $\geq 1/4$; combined with $\Pr[\mathrm{Good}]$ this yields $\Pr[\mathrm{err}(h,c_{\bar r,\bar a}) \geq 1/4] \geq \tfrac{1}{2}(1 - t/2^{d/3+2})$.

nodes.name: Adaptive vs.\ Nonadaptive SQ / Interactive vs.\ Noninteractive Local
nodes.statement: Concept classes learnable by nonadaptive SQ learners (resp.\ noninteractive local learners) under the uniform distribution are a strict subset of those learnable by adaptive SQ learners (resp.\ interactive local learners), both with and without computational restrictions.

nodes.name: Multiplicative Chernoff Bounds
nodes.statement: For i.i.d.\ Bernoulli $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ with mean $\mu$ and any $\phi \in (0,1]$: $\Pr[\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_i X_i \geq (1+\phi)\mu] \leq \exp(-\phi^2 \mu n / 3)$ and $\Pr[\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_i X_i \leq (1-\phi)\mu] \leq \exp(-\phi^2 \mu n /2)$.

nodes.name: Real-valued Additive Chernoff-Hoeffding Bound
nodes.statement: For i.i.d.\ $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ with $\mathbb{E}[X_i]=\mu$ and $a \leq X_i \leq b$: $\Pr[|\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_i X_i - \mu| \geq \delta] \leq 2\exp(-2\delta^2 n /(b-a)^2)$.

nodes.name: Sums of Laplace Random Variables
nodes.statement: For i.i.d.\ $X_i \sim \mathrm{Lap}(\lambda)$ and $\delta > 0$: $\Pr[\tfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i \geq \delta] = \exp(-\delta^2 n / (4\lambda^2))$ (under the regime $\delta < 1/2$ and $\lambda > 1$ used in the proof).

nodes.name: Private PAC Learning
nodes.statement: Given a concept class $C$ over $X$, design an algorithm that PAC-learns $C$ while satisfying $\epsilon$-differential privacy with sample complexity $\mathrm{poly}(1/\epsilon, d, 1/\alpha, \log(1/\beta))$.

nodes.name: Efficient Private vs.\ Efficient Non-private Learning
nodes.statement: It is open whether every efficiently learnable concept class is also efficiently privately learnable.

nodes.name: Distribution-Free Adaptive vs.\ Nonadaptive SQ Separation
nodes.statement: Separating adaptive from nonadaptive distribution-free SQ learning remains an open problem; MASKED-PARITY only separates them under a specific (uniform) distribution.

nodes.name: ``Anything'' Learnable is Privately Learnable
nodes.statement: If $C$ is learnable by any (not necessarily private) algorithm whose output length in bits is polynomially bounded, then $C$ is privately PAC-learnable using a polynomial number of samples (possibly in exponential time).

nodes.name: Learning with Noise vs.\ Private Learning
nodes.statement: The efficient private learner for PARITY (Theorem 4.4) shows that private learning is strictly stronger than SQ learning, dispelling the apparent equivalence between learning with noise and private learning.
